findings.reason: The diff deletes the `typeof iters[ii] === 'string'` branch, so src/Set.js:107 now passes strings to SetCollection, and src/utils/isArrayLike.js:2 treats strings as array-like, so they are iterated character by character. The packet has no story.md, so nothing on record asks for this change.
findings.claim: Removing the string special case makes Set.union split a string argument into characters instead of adding it whole, a silent behaviour change.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `if (typeof iters[ii] === 'string') { set.add(iters[ii]); } else {` and keeps only `SetCollection(iters[ii]).forEach(value => set.add(value));`. `SetCollection` treats a string as array-like (src/utils/isArrayLike.js:2 `typeof value === 'string'`), so it iterates the characters. The packet has no story.md and acceptance.md gives no criterion, so nothing on record asks for this change.

findings.reason: Every union call in __tests__/Set.ts and __tests__/OrderedSet.ts passes arrays, Sets or other collections, never a bare string, and the diff adds no test. The behaviour change in src/Set.js:107 is therefore not covered.
findings.claim: No test covers union with a string argument, so the suite passes whether strings are added whole or split.
findings.evidence: The only `union` calls in __tests__/Set.ts and __tests__/OrderedSet.ts pass arrays or Sets (e.g. line 121 `Set.union([abc, cat])`, line 261 `set.union(['a'])`, line 312 `s.union(['c'])`). None passes a string, so the deleted `typeof iters[ii] === 'string'` branch was never exercised and the diff adds no test.

findings.reason: At head, src/Set.js:103 (`this.constructor(iters[0])`) and :107 (`SetCollection(...)`) both split strings, so the inconsistency the claim describes no longer exists after this change. The part about the missing spec and test is already covered by C1 and C2.
findings.claim: union handles strings inconsistently between the empty-set shortcut and the main path.
findings.evidence: Line 102-103 `if (this.size === 0 && !this.__ownerID && iters.length === 1) { return this.constructor(iters[0]); }` sends the string to `Set(...)`, which splits it (__tests__/Set.ts:30-36 'accepts string, an array-like collection'). Line 98 `iters.filter(x => x.size !== 0)` never filters strings, because a string has no `size`. Before the change the non-empty path added the string whole while this shortcut split it. The diff makes the two paths agree without any spec or test saying which behaviour is intended.
